sources.entry: Rust: _Build your own Redis client and server_

summary.title: Tokio Tutorial: Setup
summary.one_liner: You learn what tools to install (Rust toolchain and the Mini-Redis server) before building an asynchronous Redis client and server with Tokio.
takeaways: Install the Rust toolchain (rustup is the easiest route) and confirm it with rustc --version; the tutorial needs at least Rust 1.45.0, but the latest stable is recommended.
Install the Mini-Redis server with cargo install mini-redis, then start mini-redis-server to confirm it runs.
Test the setup by running mini-redis-cli get foo in a second terminal; the expected output is (nil).
Mini-Redis is a teaching project for learning Tokio and is not a production Redis library; production-ready Redis crates are on crates.io.
summary.summary: This page is the setup step of a tutorial that walks through building a Redis client and server with Tokio, covering a subset of Redis commands and a tour of Tokio. It explains that the tutorial uses Mini-Redis, a well-commented GitHub project meant for learning Tokio, and that readers should already know Rust. The setup section covers installing Rust via rustup, checking the version, installing the mini-redis server with cargo, and verifying it with mini-redis-cli. It is a short, hands-on prerequisite page rather than a deep technical discussion.
